title: Complex tori, elliptic curves and the moduli interpretation of modular curves

results.statement: Every holomorphic map C/Lambda -> C/Lambda-prime is induced by z -> alpha z + beta with alpha Lambda contained in Lambda-prime. A pointed isomorphism has nonzero alpha and alpha Lambda = Lambda-prime.
results.state: proof supplied in this lesson; earlier prerequisites remain applicable

results.statement: The normally convergent Weierstrass series satisfies wp-prime^2 = 4 wp^3 - 60G4 wp - 140G6, has nonzero discriminant, and parametrizes the smooth cubic by a pointed biholomorphism preserving the chord-and-tangent group law.
results.state: proof supplied in this lesson; earlier prerequisites remain applicable

results.statement: For every compact connected Riemann surface X without boundary of topological genus one, every P in X and every nonzero holomorphic differential omega, the normalized functions x and y=dx/omega give a smooth cubic Y^2Z=4X0^3-aX0Z^2-bZ^3 with a^3-27b^2 nonzero and a pointed biholomorphism Phi:(X,P)->(C_ab,[0:1:0]), satisfying Phi^*(dx/y)=omega.
results.state: proved relative to the listed prerequisite foundations

results.statement: Every nonsingular complex Weierstrass cubic y^2=4x^3-a x-b is the cubic associated with a lattice with exactly those coefficients; the lattice is unique up to homothety.
results.state: proof supplied in this lesson; earlier prerequisites remain applicable

results.statement: Every compact connected pointed Riemann surface without boundary of topological genus one admits a pointed biholomorphism U=Phi_Lambda^{-1} composed with Phi to C/Lambda, with Lambda unique up to homothety.
results.state: proved relative to the listed prerequisite foundations

results.statement: Every meromorphic function on C/Lambda is uniquely R(wp)+wp-prime S(wp), with R,S in C(t); torus isogenies induce algebraic maps between the associated smooth Weierstrass cubics.
results.state: proof supplied in this lesson; earlier prerequisites remain applicable

results.statement: The analytic moduli sets of elliptic curves marked by an exact-order N point, a cyclic subgroup of order N, or a torsion basis with the specified positive determinant pairing are respectively Gamma1(N)\H, Gamma0(N)\H and Gamma(N)\H for every N>=1.
results.state: proof supplied in this lesson; earlier prerequisites remain applicable

results.statement: For n prime to cyclic level N, the normalized T_n is the quotient average 1/n over every actual order-n subgroup, retaining quotient differentials and transported level markings; it equals n^(k-1) times the index-n sublattice sum and the earlier Fourier operator.
results.state: proof supplied in this lesson; earlier prerequisites remain applicable

results.statement: The noncyclic kernel E[p] contributes p^(k-2); its intermediate subgroups give T_p^2=T_(p^2)+p^(k-1)I with the transported cyclic marking.
results.state: proof supplied in this lesson; earlier prerequisites remain applicable

remaining_requirements.statement: For every separately given smooth projective connected genus-one algebraic curve over C with a C-point, identify the analytic meromorphic coordinates of Theorem 3.0 with rational functions on that curve and prove that its analytic biholomorphism with the smooth Weierstrass cubic is an algebraic isomorphism.
affected_results: Extension of the cubic model and its algebraic moduli interpretation to a separately given algebraic genus-one curve
remaining_requirements.reason: Theorem 3.0 proves an analytic biholomorphism; Proposition 3.2 concerns displayed Weierstrass cubics and does not supply this general comparison or GAGA.

remaining_requirements.statement: Construct the appropriate Weierstrass model for a smooth projective connected genus-one curve with a rational point over an arbitrary field, retaining the characteristic-two and characteristic-three cases.
remaining_requirements.reason: The normalization y=dx/omega and the coefficient 4 proof here are over C; arbitrary-field construction is not proved.

remaining_requirements.statement: Compare the positive determinant analytic pairing (4.2), with its chosen primitive root, to the divisor-and-function algebraic Weil pairing, retaining sign conventions and arbitrary-field hypotheses.
remaining_requirements.reason: Section 4 proves the analytic convention used by Theorem 4.1; it does not prove the algebraic comparison.

remaining_requirements.statement: Supply algebraic modular-curve models over Q, reduction and Tate-module arguments with their actual base, coefficient and prime hypotheses.
remaining_requirements.reason: The lesson establishes analytic marked-curve bijections, rather than the arithmetic extensions.
